detail:
The American Heart Association describes a heart-healthy diet as one part of managing blood pressure, alongside the other lifestyle and medicine decisions a clinician makes. The pattern the Association describes is rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, low-fat dairy, lean poultry and fish, nuts, and legumes, and lower in sodium, saturated fat, and added sugars. The Association notes that foods high in sodium can raise blood pressure, and its Heart-Check mark identifies products that meet its criteria for a single serving.

The Association gives the DASH eating plan, short for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension, as the eating pattern designed specifically around blood pressure. DASH follows the same heart-healthy pattern while placing extra emphasis on limiting sodium and saturated fat. Sources present dietary change as a long-term pattern rather than a short intervention, and follow-up in the sources tracks blood pressure readings over time to judge how management is working.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing high blood pressure, diet, and medicines.
summary: The American Heart Association describes managing blood pressure with a heart-healthy eating pattern and the DASH plan, emphasizing vegetables, fruits, and whole grains while limiting sodium, saturated fat, and added sugars.
takeaways: a heart-healthy eating pattern is a foundation sources describe
the dash plan is the pattern designed around blood pressure
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Managing hypertension day to day
